description.narrative:
Stakeholders impact:
Improved access to affordable housing finance and green affordable housing finance: IFC anticipates that the investment will increase retail borrowers access to housing finance and green housing finance, and encourage homeownership for low-income segments. Rapid urbanization in India has led to several challenges including congestion, pressure on basic amenities, and severe housing shortages in cities, especially in the low-cost segment. Limited penetration of green housing is another key challenge in the housing market in India. IFC estimates a total green buildings/housing investment opportunity of US$1.4 trillion in India from 2018 to 2030.
Market impact:
Competitiveness: IFCs support to the Project, along with IFCs other systematic engagements in the affordable housing segment, will promote greater competitiveness in the affordable housing market in India, including supporting the development of green affordable housing. The housing market in India is very active with both banks as well as NBFCs and HFCs providing housing finance. However, a large proportion of the housing finance focuses on higher income groups, and low and middle-income groups remain unserved/underserved. Although IFC has been supporting the development of affordable housing financiers through continued interventions, the shortage of affordable houses and affordable housing finance is substantial and would require continuous ongoing support. In this context, the Project will demonstrate the viability of providing housing finance to lower-income groups at scale, and will also support the development of green affordable housing.

The proposed Project comprises of an up to INR 2.8 billion (approximately US$35 million) investment in Home First Finance Company Limited (Ltd) (Home First, the Company) through up to 7-year debt. The proceeds will be utilized to provide financing for retail buyers of affordable housing and green affordable housing units. The Project is expected to provide counter cyclical support for the housing needs of lower income groups, who have been severely impacted by the disruptions caused by the Covid-19 pandemic, as well as support green affordable housing, which is still underdeveloped in India, particularly in the affordable segment. Subject to internal approvals, the Project may receive support from the Market Accelerator for Green Construction (MAGC) Program as discussed in the Blended Finance Section.
